paragraphs.source_en: Kayōin pressed her prayer beads to her forehead and remained motionless for a long while. At last, she saw the true intention in Master Sessai's heart. Astonishment and gratitude surged like waves within her heart.

paragraphs.source_en: The wife of Honda Heihachirō Tadataka also had reddened eyes. Master Sessai, who wielded such immense influence within the Imagawa clan, cared more deeply for Takechiyo than even the people of Okazaki did... If her husband Tadataka, who faced death without fear, could hear all this, he would surely smile with relief.

paragraphs.source_en: “Thank you.” After a while, Kayōin said softly, “I shall do as you say and go to my daughter Odai. I will tell her not to lose her composure, no matter what happens...”

paragraphs.source_en: Kayōin left the main castle with Tadataka's wife. Autumn was deepening, and the leaves across the mountains were nearly all ablaze with red. On her way back, realization suddenly dawned upon Kayōin: she understood why Master Sessai had remained unmoved by Sumpu's repeated demands that he hasten. He meant to wait until the autumn harvest was finished; beyond doubt, he was waiting for the common folk on both sides, friend and foe alike, to reap safely the fruits of an entire year's toil.

paragraphs.source_en: Kayōin's surmise was correct. Seven-tenths of the autumn harvest was now complete, and the rice fields were gradually growing bare.

paragraphs.source_en: Just as the two women, stumbling through a steady drizzle, were about to cross the Yahagi River, the sudden call of war horns rang out from Okazaki Castle. The tense standoff that had endured since the third month of Tenbun 18 was about to erupt into a decisive battle. Did the fierce commander Oda Nobuhide intend to seize Okazaki Castle in a single stroke? Or would Master Sessai, the very backbone of the Imagawa clan, crush Nobuhide's elite forces and capture Anshō Castle? Both sides were determined to prevail. Their victory or defeat would determine the fate of Matsudaira Takechiyo.
